title: Translation of input-position sources
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine with $k$ work tapes, and let $N,T,t,p\in\mathbb N$. Let $\ell$ be a list of bit-source descriptors with $|\ell|=N$, and assume $p<N+2$. For a valuation $\rho$ of the eleven registers, assume its $I$ register equals the encoded index of input position $p$ at time $t$, its $Q$ register equals the encoded index of position $p$ at time $t-1$ whenever $t\ne0$, and its $LB$ register equals $t$ times the configuration stride. Choose a layout value among $0,1,2$, and assume its associated source translates to the source from $\ell$ at position $p$ when $1\le p\le N$, and to the false constant otherwise. Then translating each descriptor in the input-position source list (formed using the snapshot width, $t$, $p$, and this layout value) gives exactly the canonical source list for input position $p$ at time $t$, including its neighboring input and previous-snapshot sources.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over the binary alphabet
$\ell$ is a list of bit-source descriptors
$\rho$ is a valuation of the eleven registers
$\rho(I)$ is the encoded index of input position $p$ at time $t$
if $t\ne0$, $\rho(Q)$ is the encoded index of input position $p$ at time $t-1$
the translated layout source equals the indicated hard-wired source or false constant
caveat: The claim is an exact equality of two specifically constructed lists, and the supplied descriptions do not define the source-translation and list-construction notation. The prose summarizes the equality and its hypotheses, but cannot spell out every list entry without effectively reproducing those definitions.
